title: Elohim-civilization hypothesis
statement: The beings Wheel of Heaven identifies as the Elohim were a technologically advanced biological civilization from elsewhere and were responsible for designing terrestrial life, including humanity.

includes: The biological and civilizational character attributed to the Elohim
The proposed off-world origin of the civilization
The proposed design of terrestrial life and humanity
excludes: The report layer itself — what the canonical source explicitly states — which is recorded by woh-claim-0070
Every detail reported by the Raëlian corpus
The present location, population, governance, motives, or lifespan of the proposed civilization

alternatives.statement: Relevant uses of Elohim designate divine beings within theological and literary traditions rather than an extraterrestrial civilization.
Biblical plurality and divine-council language are better explained by the historical development of ancient Israelite religion.
The Raëlian contact report is better explained by literary, revelatory, psychological, sociological, fictional, mistaken, or other non-extraterrestrial accounts.
The origin and development of terrestrial life require no technologically directed intervention.

revision_triggers: The canonical contact report record (woh-claim-0070) materially changes.
The identification of biblical Elohim with the reported civilization changes independently of the biological-civilization proposition.
A reproducible review materially changes the relevant philological, historical, biological, or source-critical evidence map.
A review of the biblical-identification or design-of-life subclaims advances toward reviewed, triggering the full four-way decomposition deferred by ADR 0007.
A public derivative strengthens, narrows, or contradicts this proposition.
